title: The World of AI: Legal Models catalogue from Hugging Face Hub
answer: This is The World of AI page for Legal Models, a catalogue of the 1000 most downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub. It lists licence, downloads and release date, refreshed daily from the Hub public API and sorted by all time downloads. Each model links to its own Hub page. The most useful thing is that it offers a dated, citable index of open legal models, last verified 2026-09-27, for readers tracking legal models.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page at theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/technology-and-core-infrastructure/9933cd93/. It is a catalogue page for Legal Models, not a long form article. Its stated scope is the 1000 most downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads and release date, refreshed daily. The page says its source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, refreshed daily, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It carries a last verified date of 2026-09-27. The same text also says the wider site searches the full text of every published page, all built from the same database, including state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators and weekly digests.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents a daily refreshed index of open legal models. It says the catalogue covers the 1000 most downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub and gives licence, downloads and release date for each. The data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page also explains that the wider site searches the full text of every published page, all built from the same database. That database includes state AI laws, the lawsuit tracker, the glossary, the tools directory, AI companies, the research library, the MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, the calculators and the weekly digests. It describes itself as an atlas of artificial intelligence, covering what the law says, who is suing whom and what the words mean. It says every page is rebuilt daily from primary sources and carries the date it was last verified, and that it is free to read, free to cite and free to query. The page also includes notes about books and services. It says books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, are available on Amazon. It announces that SRJ Consulting & Services has published its first work of fiction on AI, The AI Lawyer, a novel, out 17 August 2026. It also lists service names such as the AI Business Enablement Audit and the AI Risk and Governance Review.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the catalogue covers the 1000 most downloaded open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub. It states that the data is refreshed daily and comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads. It gives a last verified date of 2026-09-27. It says every model links to its own Hub page. It says the wider site is rebuilt daily from primary sources and is free to read, free to cite and free to query. It gives 17 August 2026 as the publication date for The AI Lawyer, a novel by SRJ Consulting & Services. It does not give individual download counts, licence names or model names in the supplied text.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in the Legal industry would use this source as a discovery and citation point for open legal models. The page tracks open legal models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads and release date, refreshed daily. That helps a reader see which open models are most downloaded and when they were released, without needing to query the Hub directly. The page also places this catalogue inside a wider database that includes a lawsuit tracker, state AI laws, a glossary and compliance frameworks, so it can act as an entry point to related legal AI material on the same site. It is not an analysis of model quality or legal fitness, but it is a dated index that can be cited and checked.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: This is a catalogue and landing page, not a full article or evaluation. The supplied text does not list the models, their licences, download counts or release dates, so it cannot support detailed comparison on its own. It gives no benchmarks, accuracy measures or legal use cases. It is partly commercial, promoting books by Stephen R. Jordan and services from SRJ Consulting & Services. It is dated by its last verified date of 2026-09-27 and relies on the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads. The wider site claims daily rebuilding from primary sources, but this page itself offers only a short description.
